lens: VLDB/TKDE reviewer lens: TRACQ cannot and should not fight ZFP/SZ3 on absolute-RMSE-at-ratio for smooth unit-scale fields — that is their home turf and the current open-loop cumprod design loses by construction. The regime where a relative-change image grid can honestly win is POINTWISE RELATIVE-ERROR-BOUNDED lossy compression of MULTI-SCALE multivariate sensor data at FULL per-timestep resolution. The winning metrics are (a) rate at a fixed max relative error / SMAPE / per-channel NRMSE, and (b) guaranteed per-point bounds, where ZFP's tolerance mode is absolute-only (it must set tol for the smallest-magnitude channel, wasting bits on kilounit channels, or blow 10-100% relative error on near-unit channels like UCI CO ~0.5-2 mg/m3 next to PT08 sensors ~800-2000), PAA-1024 destroys per-timestep detail (its RMSE 1.55 hides that every within-segment transient is gone — report per-timestep max error and it collapses), and Gorilla/Delta+Zstd are lossless so their 0.12-0.24 ratios are the floor TRACQ must undercut 3-5x. The current implementation loses for one dominant, verifiable reason: `core.py`/`core_enhanced.py` compute pct changes OPEN-LOOP from the original data and reconstruct by `np.cumprod` (core_enhanced.py:634-636), so per-step quantization error compounds multiplicatively without bound (MetroPT-3 RMSE 3.8e95). Everything else (mu-law, adaptive clamp, anchors) is patching that wound. Fix the loop, add a real error bound in the log-ratio domain, sharpen the symbol distribution with a predictor, and stop wasting the entropy stage — then the rate-at-fixed-relative-error tables favor TRACQ honestly.
overall_assessment: Proposal 1 (closed-loop DPCM) matters most — it is the sine qua non: without it every other change is polishing a diverging codec, and with it anchors (and their bytes) disappear and per-point error becomes bounded by one quantization step. But P1 alone only stops losing; the combination that WINS the resubmission is P1 + P2 + P4: closed-loop encoding in the log-ratio domain with a user-specified pointwise relative-error bound and sparse exact-value exceptions, entropy-coded as a bit-packed/Zstd symbol plane with the PNG kept as the viewable artifact. That package converts TRACQ from 'lossy method barely smaller than lossless Delta+Zstd' (0.05-0.22 vs 0.12-0.24) into a guaranteed-relative-error codec at roughly 0.02-0.06 ratio, and it enables the two tables ZFP structurally cannot win: rate at fixed max-relative-error on multi-scale data, and SMAPE/per-channel-NRMSE vs ratio Pareto fronts — while the per-timestep resolution axis kills PAA and the lossy-vs-lossless size axis kills Gorilla. P3 (order-2 predictor with per-variable selection) is a solid 15-35% rate bonus to add if the schedule allows, ideally framed as an ablation. Benchmark honestly: include absolute RMSE tables too (TRACQ will still lose some of those to ZFP on single-scale channels — say so), run ZFP both on the 2D grid and per-channel-1D, and run SZ3 in REL mode as the strongest fair competitor; TRACQ's differentiators that survive that comparison are the guaranteed pointwise relative bound, the multi-scale win, and the image-viewable compressed-domain artifact that none of the competitors provide.

proposals.name: Closed-loop (DPCM) encoding — kill the cumprod drift
proposals.mechanism: Encode each relative change against the DECODER's reconstruction instead of the original: maintain x_hat[i] in the encoder; at step t compute p[i,t] = 100*(x[i,t] - x_hat[i]) / max(|x_hat[i]|, eps), clamp, mu-law, quantize, then IMMEDIATELY dequantize inside the encoder and update x_hat[i] = x_hat[i]*(1 + p_hat[i,t]/100). Decode is unchanged (same cumulative recursion), but now the encoder has already absorbed each step's quantization error into the next step's symbol, so error never compounds: per-point relative error is bounded by ~one quantizer step (mu-law step near center ≈ clamp*ln(1+mu)/(mu*2^(b-1)) percent; for clamp=20%, mu=255, 8-bit ≈ 0.09%). Anchors become dead weight and are removed.
proposals.why_it_wins: This is the classic DPCM closed-loop result: open-loop quantization noise in a first-order recursive decoder accumulates as a random walk (variance grows ~linearly in t in the log domain, i.e., multiplicatively in value domain — hence MetroPT-3's RMSE 3.8e95 over 1.5M steps), while closed-loop bounds the error of EVERY reconstructed point to one quantization step regardless of T. It also deletes the anchor side-channel: at anchor_interval=100 on MetroPT-3 (15 vars, 1.5M steps), anchors cost ~15*15000*8 B ≈ 1.8 MB of exact float64 — a large fraction of the 0.0297 ratio's byte budget — for a problem that closed-loop solves for free.
proposals.expected_gain: MetroPT-3 unanchored: RMSE 3.8e95 → finite and comparable to the anchored 1.71, at a ratio that DROPS from 0.0297 toward ~0.019-0.022 because the 1.8 MB anchor payload disappears. UCI Air Quality 8-bit: RMSE 108.3 → roughly the per-step bound times channel magnitude, i.e., O(0.1-1) instead of O(100) — a 2-3 order-of-magnitude RMSE reduction at slightly better ratio (no anchors). This single change moves TRACQ from 'diverges' to 'on the Pareto chart'.
proposals.implementation_sketch: In tracq/core_enhanced.py replace the vectorized open-loop path (_compute_raw_percent_grid + quantize_8bit/quantize_16bit) with an encode loop: vectorize across the n_vars axis, iterate t=1..T-1 in Python (each iteration does O(n_vars) numpy work: pct vs x_hat, clip to precomputed per-var clamps, _COMPANDER.compress, round to uint, then expand/declamp and x_hat update). Precompute clamps from the open-loop pct grid as today (clamps are metadata either way). Gate a numba.njit kernel behind the existing HAS_NUMBA flag for the 1.5M-step datasets (pure-Python loop is ~5-15 s for 1.5M x 15, numba ~0.1 s). Delete the anchor branches in quantize_*bit and the anchor re-propagation block in reconstruct_from_quantized (lines 639-657). Decode path needs no change beyond ignoring anchors.
proposals.risk: Encoder becomes sequential — encode throughput drops vs the current vectorized cumprod path (mitigated by numba; report honest encode MB/s). Clamp saturation: if the signal moves faster than the clamp allows, closed-loop tracks it over several steps (slew-rate limiting) instead of diverging, but a transient can exceed the nominal per-step bound — fixed properly by Proposal 2's exception mechanism. Near-zero x_hat still needs the epsilon/auto-offset guard.
proposals.interactions: Prerequisite for everything else: P2's error bound is only meaningful closed-loop; P3's predictor must predict from RECONSTRUCTED history (same loop, one extra state vector); P4 benefits because closed-loop symbols are better centered. Conflicts with nothing; obsoletes the anchor mechanism and most of the auto-offset heuristics' urgency.
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: The stored artifact is still exactly one uint8/uint16 pixel per (variable, timestep) — same shape, same PNG container, same visual semantics (bright/dark = large up/down relative move). Only the values the encoder writes change; viewability and compressed-domain anomaly detection are untouched.

proposals.name: Log-ratio domain with user-specified pointwise relative-error bound + sparse exceptions
proposals.mechanism: Replace the pct-change formula with symmetric log-ratios encoded closed-loop, and replace fixed 8/16-bit mu-law with an SZ-style fixed-step quantizer derived from a user bound eb: r[i,t] = ln(|x[i,t]| / max(|x_hat[i]|, eps)); symbol k = round(r / (2*ln(1+eb))); x_hat updated as x_hat * exp(2k*ln(1+eb)) * sign. By construction every reconstructed point satisfies |x_hat - x|/|x| <= eb exactly (the log-domain analogue of SZ3's linear-quantization bound). Symbols are stored center-shifted in the uint8/uint16 grid; any point whose symbol overflows the grid range, changes sign, or hits the near-zero guard is written as the center code (0 = 'exception') and its exact float64 value appended to a sparse exception list (indices + values) in the container. Log domain also removes the +5%/-5% asymmetry bias the current pct formula has.
proposals.why_it_wins: This creates the operating mode the paper was rejected for lacking (brief failure #5) and targets ZFP's structural weakness: zfpy tolerance mode is ABSOLUTE-error only, so on UCI Air Quality (channels spanning ~0.5 to ~2000) it either wastes bits meeting tol=1e-1 on kilounit channels or commits 5-20% relative error on the CO/benzene channels. TRACQ with eb=1% guarantees 1% on every channel and every timestep. Information-theoretically, hourly sensor log-ratios are Laplacian with scale ~0.005-0.05, so at step 2*ln(1.01)≈0.0199 the symbol entropy is ~1.5-3 bits — far below the 8 bits currently stored — which is what finally separates lossy TRACQ from lossless Delta+Zstd (failure #3).
proposals.expected_gain: UCI Air Quality at eb=1%: ~2-3 bits/symbol after P4's entropy stage → ratio ~0.03-0.06 vs float64 (down from 0.114) with guaranteed max relative error 1% and SMAPE <= ~1% — undercutting lossless Delta+Zstd (0.12-0.24) by 3-5x and beating ZFP on max-relative-error at equal rate by 1-2 orders of magnitude on the small-magnitude channels. MetroPT-3 at eb=0.5%: expected ratio ~0.01-0.02 with per-point 0.5% bound — Pareto-dominant over anchored TRACQ (1.71 @ 0.0297) and qualitatively different from PAA (which has NO per-timestep guarantee at all). Enables the headline table: 'bytes per point at fixed max relative error' where only SZ3-REL is a real competitor.
proposals.implementation_sketch: Add error_bound: Optional[float] to EnhancedTimeSeriesGrid.__init__; when set, the P1 encode loop uses step=2*np.log1p(eb) on r=np.log(np.abs(x_t)/np.abs(x_hat)) (all vectorized across vars inside the t-loop), k=np.rint(r/step), overflow/sign-change/near-zero mask → exception. Store grid as uint8 if max|k|<128 else uint16, center-shifted (+128/+32768). Exceptions: two arrays (flat int64 indices, float64 values) — serialize as base64 in the existing tEXt JSON for small counts or as a Zstd side-blob in container.py for large ones. Decode: k → x_hat *= np.exp(k*step) cumulatively (vectorized cumsum in log domain now that it is closed-loop-safe), then scatter exceptions. Reuse the existing auto-offset machinery to pre-lift zero-crossing channels and keep exception density low. Benchmark via scripts/rate_distortion.py sweeping eb in {5%,2%,1%,0.5%,0.1%} against zfp_sweep tolerance mode and sz3_sweep rel mode.
proposals.risk: Exception density is the failure mode: a channel that oscillates through zero (some MetroPT-3 analog channels) could generate 10-30% exceptions and destroy the ratio — mitigate with the existing auto_offset lift plus a per-variable fallback to absolute-delta coding (flag in metadata) when the exception rate on a prefix exceeds ~2%. Second risk: reviewers will note relative-bound codecs lose absolute-RMSE tables on single-scale data; the paper must present both and claim the multi-scale/relative regime explicitly, with SZ3-REL included as the fair strongest baseline.
proposals.interactions: Requires P1 (bound only holds closed-loop). Synergizes strongly with P4: fixed-step symbols at eb=1% occupy few distinct values, so bit-packing + Zstd realizes the 1.5-3 bit entropy. P3 plugs in upstream (predict r, quantize the residual with the same step — bound still holds because the decoder applies the same prediction). Largely supersedes mu-law for the error-bounded mode (mu-law remains for the fixed-budget 8-bit mode); reduces reliance on adaptive clamp heuristics.
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: The symbol grid is still one pixel per (variable, timestep), stored in the same PNG path; mid-gray = 'no change', brightness = magnitude of relative move — visually identical semantics to today, and exceptions render as a distinct sentinel value (visible as marked pixels, which is itself useful for inspection). No downsampling anywhere.

proposals.name: Order-2 predictor on reconstructed history (delta-of-delta in log-ratio domain), per-variable selection
proposals.mechanism: Inside the closed-loop encoder, before quantization, subtract a prediction of the current log-ratio from the reconstructed past: r_pred[i,t] = r_hat[i,t-1] (i.e., predict 'same relative change as last step' — equivalent to linear extrapolation in log-value, the 1D Lorenzo/Gorilla delta-of-delta idea), and quantize the residual e = r - r_pred with the P2 step. The decoder forms the same prediction from its own history and adds the dequantized residual, so the eb guarantee is unchanged. Choose per variable between predictor order 0 (encode r directly — best for white-noise-like channels) and order 1 (delta-of-delta — best for smooth/trending channels) by measuring residual entropy on the data during encode; store 1 flag byte per variable.
proposals.why_it_wins: This is exactly the mechanism that makes SZ3 and Gorilla small: smooth sensor channels (temperature, humidity, pressure — most of UCI and MetroPT-3) have strongly autocorrelated increments, so Var(e) is 2-5x below Var(r), which is ~0.5-1.2 bits/symbol of entropy reduction at fixed step size. TRACQ currently uses only the order-1 'previous value' predictor (brief root-cause #2), leaving that redundancy on the table for PNG DEFLATE, which cannot model it across a row. Moving the redundancy removal from the entropy coder into the predictor is worth strictly more than hoping DEFLATE finds it.
proposals.expected_gain: On smooth channels, 20-40% rate reduction at identical error bound (e.g., UCI at eb=1%: ~2.5 bits/symbol → ~1.6-2.0 bits/symbol → ratio 0.04 → ~0.028); on noisy channels ~0% (order-0 fallback prevents regression, cost 1 byte/var). Net dataset-level gain estimated 15-35% on UCI Air Quality and MetroPT-3 — this is the margin that turns 'competitive with SZ3-REL' into 'beats or ties SZ3-REL' at 1-2% bounds, and it directly improves BOTH axes of every rate-distortion figure.
proposals.implementation_sketch: In the P1/P2 encode loop keep one extra state vector r_hat_prev (n_vars,); compute e = r - flags*r_hat_prev (flags is the 0/1 per-var predictor vector, so it stays fully vectorized across vars); quantize e, dequantize, set r_hat_prev = flags*r_hat_prev + e_hat... i.e., reconstructed r. Selection pass: encode the first min(T, 20000) steps both ways (cheap, same loop), pick per-var the lower sum of |symbol| (proxy for entropy); store "predictor": [0,1,1,0,...] in metadata. Decode mirrors with the same state vector. ~60 lines of change, no new dependencies; numba kernel extends trivially.
proposals.risk: On channels where increments are near-white (some MetroPT-3 pressure sensors during idle), order-1 prediction DOUBLES residual variance — the per-variable selection flag is mandatory, not optional. Slight decode complexity increase. Prediction from reconstructed (not original) history is essential; predicting from originals would silently reintroduce open-loop drift — a subtle implementation bug to guard with a long-horizon drift test (encode 1M steps, assert max rel error <= eb).
proposals.interactions: Pure upstream synergy with P2 (same quantizer, bound preserved) and P4 (residual symbols are even more concentrated, so bit-packing/Zstd gain more). Requires P1's loop structure. Slightly reduces the visual 'trend' content of the image (see artifact note) — a fair trade the paper should show side-by-side.
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: Still one pixel per (variable, timestep). The image becomes a PREDICTION-RESIDUAL map: mid-gray = 'behaved as expected', bright/dark pixels = surprises. For compressed-domain anomaly detection this is strictly better than the raw pct grid (anomalies pop against a flat background); the paper can sell this as a feature with a before/after figure, and channels using order-0 look identical to today.

proposals.name: Entropy stage: bit-packed symbol plane + Zstd, PNG kept as the viewable artifact
proposals.mechanism: Stop measuring TRACQ's size as 'PNG DEFLATE over a full-range mu-law grid'. After P2/P3 the symbol plane has few distinct values concentrated at center; exploit it three ways: (1) sub-byte bit-packing when max|k| fits 2/4 bits (np.packbits on interleaved nibbles); (2) Zstd level 19 over the packed row-major plane (rows = variables, so runs within a channel stay contiguous) as the archival encoding; (3) still emit the PNG (with compress_level=9, optimize=True, and Pillow's filter search) as the viewable artifact, and report both sizes explicitly — 'archive' bytes (Zstd) for the rate-distortion tables and 'viewable' bytes (PNG) in a separate honesty column. Optionally add a zero-run RLE pre-pass for channels that are constant for long stretches (common in MetroPT-3 idle periods).
proposals.why_it_wins: The brief's root-cause #3 verified in code: codec.py stores the raw grid via Pillow PNG default filters, and mu-law deliberately spreads symbols across [0,255], so DEFLATE finds almost no skew — TRACQ currently pays ~8 bits/point when the post-P2/P3 symbol entropy is 1.5-3 bits. Zstd's FSE entropy stage approaches the empirical symbol entropy; DEFLATE's Huffman-on-LZ77 does not on near-incompressible-looking planes. This is the cheapest 2-4x in the whole plan and it is what finally makes the lossy-vs-lossless comparison (failure #3) decisive.
proposals.expected_gain: At eb=1% on UCI: 8 bits/point stored → ~2-3 bits/point effective → additional 2.5-4x ratio improvement on top of P2 (combined ratio ~0.03-0.05, and ~0.02-0.03 with P3). On MetroPT-3 idle-heavy channels the zero-run pass can push below 1 bit/point. PNG-optimized artifact typically lands 10-25% above the Zstd size — small enough that the viewable artifact remains a credible deliverable rather than an asterisk.
proposals.implementation_sketch: In tracq/container.py (Zstd path already exists per the brief): add pack_symbols(q, bits_needed) using np.packbits / manual nibble interleave; compress with zstandard.ZstdCompressor(level=19); metadata gains {"packing": bits, "entropy_stage": "zstd19"}. In codec.py save_png: pass optimize=True, compress_level=9 (one-line change). Add a tracq/entropy.py helper that returns both encodings and their sizes so scripts/realworld_benchmark.py and rate_distortion.py can report archive-vs-viewable columns honestly. Zero-run pre-pass: split each row into (run-lengths of center symbol, literals), both Zstd'd — ~40 lines, guarded by a per-dataset win check.
proposals.risk: Low technical risk; the main risk is presentational — reviewers may object if the paper quotes Zstd sizes while claiming an image artifact. Mitigate by reporting both columns in every table and noting the PNG is within 10-25%; alternatively make PNG-with-optimized-filters the primary number and Zstd the 'archival mode'. RLE pre-pass adds a format variant to maintain — keep it flag-gated.
proposals.interactions: Multiplies P2/P3's gains (they create the skew this stage cashes in); nearly worthless without them (today's mu-law grid is deliberately full-range). No conflict with P1. Also improves the fixed-budget 8-bit mu-law mode slightly (10-20%) via PNG optimize + Zstd choice.
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: Explicitly dual-container: the PNG (one pixel per variable-timestep) is always produced and is the viewable artifact; the bit-packed Zstd blob is a byte-exact re-encoding of the same grid for archival/rate reporting. Nothing about the grid geometry or per-timestep resolution changes; a user can always materialize the PNG from the blob losslessly.
